title: Minimum Cost of a Path With Special Roads
summary: Given an initial position and a target position in a 2D space, along with the cost of moving between any two points and a set of special roads with their own costs, determine the minimum cost to reach the target using any number of special roads.
statement: Given an initial position and a target position in a 2D space, along with the cost of moving between any two points and a set of special roads with their own costs, determine the minimum cost to reach the target using any number of special roads.
constraints: Ordinary travel between any two integer-coordinate points costs their Manhattan distance.
A directed special road [x1,y1,x2,y2,cost] may be used any number of times after ordinary travel to its start.
Return the minimum total cost from start to target.
hints: Treat the start and every special-road endpoint as shortest-path states.
From a state, update the direct Manhattan route to target.
For every special road, pay Manhattan distance to its start plus road cost, and relax its endpoint in Dijkstra’s heap.
Any optimal route alternates ordinary segments with special roads; each alternation is represented, and nonnegative costs make Dijkstra finalization valid.
editorial: Any optimal route alternates ordinary segments with special roads; each alternation is represented, and nonnegative costs make Dijkstra finalization valid.

tests.explanation: Ordinary movement into the two special roads produces minimum total cost five.
Combining useful directed roads and ordinary movement costs five.
